newsitem.title: GERMANY: German TV station Pro Sieben plans July IPO.
newsitem.headline: German TV station Pro Sieben plans July IPO.

text.p: German private television channel Pro Sieben Media AG is scheduling its initial public offering for the first half of July and plans to raise over one billion marks from the IPO, a newspaper said on Saturday.

Pro Sieben will become the first German television station with a stock market listing. It plans to raise over one billion marks from the flotation and will combine the IPO with a 25 million-mark capital raise, Boersenzeitung said in a report.

The group said it plans to list preference shares when it comes to market. The main shareholder will be Thomas Kirch, son of Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch, who will retain 60 percent of ordinary shares.
The other main shareholder will be the Cologne-based retail group Rewe AG, with 40 percent. Bookbuilding, where the flotation price will be set, is to begin in TNE third week of June.
The group previously shelved plans for a 1996 flotation.
"An extra year of preparation time and consideration have been to our advantage. It's good for us to come to market now," chairman Georg Koefler told Boersenzeitung.
Sales at the parent group in 1996 grew to 1.6 billion marks from 1.47 billion marks in 1995, while the group saw double-digit growth in sales and profits, the report said.
